question: Citrus canker is a:
solution:
The correct answer is a __**bacterial disease**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Citrus canker is a bacterial disease caused by the bacterium Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri: 
 
• Symptoms
 
• Citrus canker causes lesions on the leaves, stems, and fruit of citrus plants. The leaves may drop and unripe fruit may fall to the ground. 
 
• Impact
 
• Citrus canker affects the health of infected citrus trees and the marketability of infected fruit. While not harmful to humans, there is no cure for citrus canker. 
 
• Spread
 
• Citrus canker is most severe in hot, wet areas. It is highly contagious and can affect all above-ground parts of citrus trees. 
 
• Control
 
 
• To control citrus canker, you can:
 
• Reduce wind speeds with windbreaks 
 
• Apply copper sprays to the fruit and leaves 
 
• Practice sanitation 
 
• Control leafminer
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Hormonal Disorder:
 
 
• A hormonal disorder refers to an imbalance or abnormality in the hormones in the body.
 
• Hormones are chemicals produced by glands and regulate various functions in the body, including growth, metabolism, and mood.
 
• Disorders like hypothyroidism, diabetes, and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) are examples of hormonal disorders.
 
 
 
• Viral Disease:
 
 
• A viral disease is an illness caused by a virus, a microscopic agent that requires a living host to replicate.
 
• Viral infections can affect various parts of the body, such as the respiratory system (e.g., the flu), the digestive system (e.g., gastroenteritis), or the skin (e.g., chickenpox).
 
• Viruses can sometimes lead to chronic conditions, like HIV/AIDS.
 
 
 
• Fungal Disease:
 
 
• A **fungal disease** is an infection caused by fungi.
 
• Fungi are microorganisms that can live in the environment or on the skin and mucous membranes.
 
• When they grow out of control, they can cause diseases like athlete's foot, ringworm, and candidiasis (yeast infections).
